brief: JPMorgan Market Intelligence moves to a Tactically Cautious / Neutral stance: fundamentals stay strong but six near-term variables should chop markets sideways for 2-3 weeks. Warsh's comments make September a live meeting, with CPI on Sep 11 the more important input than Friday's payrolls because Warsh views the US as at full employment. Positioning gives no clean read and implies 3-4 choppy weeks, post-Labor Day issuance widens credit spreads which pressures equities, September screens as the worst SPX month, Momentum (JPMPURE) is down over 21% and Classic Momentum (JPPQMO) nearly 34% from June highs versus a typical 10-15% drawdown, and AVGO earnings may be spectacular without lifting AI, Memory and Semis. That argues for reducing net-longs and potentially a dollar-neutral or market-neutral approach. Today: SPX -0.6%, WTI +2.6% to $93.39 on Houthi strikes and US strikes near Kharg Island, SOXX +1.6% on OpenAI's Astra release while software fell 2.3%. The Aug 31 menu starts long NDX versus short RTY.
